activity.title: 🚀 Just wrapped up an incredible 12-week journey as a Software Engineering Intern at Ubitus K.K. in Taiwan! This experience pushed me far beyond my comfort zone and taught me that engineering is about so much more than just coding--it's about solving complex problems and thinking systematically. 🔍 Key Achievements: • Built a semantic search MCP server for our company LLM, achieving 77.8% F1 Score with cross-collection capabilities • Developed a company-wide prompt injection defense framework that blocked 100% of attacks across 5 AI applications • Operated the G1 humanoid robot at AI WAVE exhibition, bridging technical implementation with real-world demonstrations 🧠 Beyond the Technical: The most transformative part? Deep conversations with manager Vic and mentor Melody about what defines an engineer. They showed me that coding is simply "描述事情的邏輯，是將邏輯具象化的工具" - the description of logical processes; it serves as a tool for concretizing abstract logic. Sometimes the best solution isn't writing more code, but finding the right people and approach to solve the problem. From discussing AI consciousness to exploring philosophical questions about adaptation and existence, this internship expanded my thinking in ways I never expected. I am extremely grateful to the people I met here, especially Ubitus - TP Vic Chiang , for your invaluable insights and creativity, and for teaching me how to tell a story and express ideas fully to listeners. A huge shoutout to my supportive mentor Melody Wang for your guidance and patience. Without Hung-Yi Shih 's and Andy Khoo Yuen Khai 's help, things couldn't have gone this well at the AI WAVE exhibition. Thank you also to Helen Lyu for exposing me to the work in the Marketing and BD team. Thank you to the entire RD/TDG/CNF team for making these 12 weeks the most memorable experience of my life. The insights and perspectives I've gained will carry forward into everything I build next. #Ubitus #SoftwareEngineering #AI #MachineLearning #Internship #Taiwan #TechCareers #PersonalGrowth #Milvus #VectorDB #RAG ...more

Thrilled to share my experience representing Ubitus K.K. at Taiwan's largest AI exhibition - #WAVE2025 ! It was an honor to showcase our company's cutting-edge products to such an engaged audience. I had the incredible opportunity to be at the forefront of our showcase, controlling our AI Humanoid with an Apple Vision Pro. This interactive demo wasn't just about handing out snacks; we were actively gathering valuable training data for the robot's future Reinforcement Learning models. The positive energy and interest our booth attracted were fantastic! We demonstrated our suite of AI solutions: 🤖 AI Humanoid: An AI companion designed for healthcare settings like Mackey Memorial Hospital, capable of patient interaction, physical support, and specimen delivery. 🐳 UbiOne: A dynamic platform for creating and interacting with customizable virtual characters who can chat, dance, and generate images. It supports voice interaction, multilingual communication, and emotional expression, making it perfect for VTubers, customer service, and brand characters. 🎨 UbiArt: A powerful tool for AI-powered image and video generation with 22 style transformations. By combining natural language prompts with the Diffusion model, it can quickly generate unique illustrations and animations. 😊 UbiReal: Our 8K hyper-real avatars. The integration of Unreal Engine and NVIDIA ACE achieves extremely realistic appearance and voice-synchronized expressions, allowing visitors to experience immersive virtual interactions. Interacting with visitors and hearing their feedback on our products was invaluable. Exploring the expo, I observed key industry trends focused on virtual characters, diverse AI agent applications, robotics, and computer vision. It was inspiring to connect with other innovators in the field. A huge thank you to Amy Huang , Andy Khoo Yuen Khai , Helen Lyu, Hung-Yi Shih . Their guidance has been instrumental in my learning journey, providing me with a holistic view of the AI industry, more specifically in the difference between Business Development, Marketing, Sales, and R&D teams. #AI #Ubitus #Internship #AIWAVE #Robotics #GenerativeAI #VirtualCharacters #ReinforcementLearning #AppleVisionPro #TechExpo ...more

This June I graduated from the University of California, Santa Barbara with a B.S. in Applied Statistics & Data Science! After learning the theory and math behind machine learning algorithms and building hands-on projects like applying unsupervised machine learning to cluster players based on their performance and play styles and training CNNs to flag AI images versus real ones, I realized I enjoy the creativity of software engineering and the satisfaction you get when something you've built finally works exactly how you pictured it. With that, I've decided to pursue a Master's in Computer Science at the University of California, Irvine. Thank you UCSB for the best two years of my life, and all the memories and friends I made along the way. On to the next at University of California, Irvine !

With great joy and pride, and after countless late nights and years of hard work, I am thrilled to announce my graduation from UC Santa Barbara with a Bachelor of Science in Statistics and Data Science. None of this would have been possible without the endless support of my incredible family, friends, and amazing professors along the way! Thank you for believing in me every step of the way. I'm also planning to begin my journey toward starting a Master's program in Business Analytics or Statistics/Applied Mathematics at the UC system. I look forward to diving deep into the program, expanding my skill set, and connecting with industry leaders and peers. I guess the tassel was worth the hassle!

At Runpod 's Flash Hack Day in SF today, I built a World Cup simulator that can run millions of tournament simulations in parallel on Runpod's Serverless GPU platform. I pulled a the past decade's worth of FIFA match data, about ~43,000 games, and trained a neural network on Colab to predict match outcomes. Then I deployed it on Runpod, where every simulated match is a NN forward pass. Run 1 million tournament simulations, and you're running 100s of millions of inferences across a GPU swarm that scales up from zero, and back down when it's done. Thank you Dean for letting me know this event was happening! Runpod HackerSquad

Thank you, Prof. Kiana Aran, for encouraging me to take this opportunity and for training me to be capable of it. Thank you, Dr. Walter Alvarado, PhD (in picture) for choosing me for this position. I would also like to thank my recommenders, Prof. Shriya Srinivasan , Prof. Andrew McCulloch , Prof. Will Styler and Dr. Deependra Kumar Ban , for their recommendation letters. Thank you as well to Prof. Adam Engler , Bioengineering Chair at UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering , Hannibal Barake from The National GEM Consortium, and Edgar Beas at UC San Diego for making this opportunity possible for me. I am honoured to work with scientists Dr. Antonio Ricco , Dr. Piyumi Wijesekara , and Dr. Mary Beth Wilhelm here at the NASA AMES. I also had a warm start meeting fellow interns Rushil Gupta , Hannah G. Simon , Tiffany Hoang , Morgan Rafferty and Internships Coordinator Katie T. Here's to a summer of science, curiosity, and stepping a little closer to the stars.
